1	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, drawing into the existing canvas with id #app (640x360 CSS pixels; do not resize it or add another canvas). Make a complete small 3D pointer-driven reaction game.
2	
3	Rules:
4	1. A 3 by 3 grid of holes or pedestals is shown in the scene. Every so often one glowing lantern (or another simple object of your choice) pops up from a random cell, stays visible for a short time that gets shorter as the score rises, then drops back down.
5	2. Clicking or tapping a raised lantern pops it: +10 points, with a visible burst or flash. Clicking an empty cell or a lantern that is already lowered costs 5 points (score never goes below 0) and gives visible feedback. A hover highlight shows which cell the pointer is over.
6	3. Occasionally a different colored bomb object appears instead; clicking it ends the run with status `lost`. Letting a normal lantern drop without popping it does not cost lives.
7	4. The round lasts 45 seconds. When the timer reaches 0 the status is `won` if the score is at least 150, otherwise `lost`. The game starts in status `ready` and begins on the first click on a Start button or the Enter key.
8	5. R, or a Restart button shown on the end overlay, begins a new round (score 0, timer 45, status `playing`). Use a seeded random generator so a seed repeats the spawn order.
9	6. A DOM HUD outside the canvas shows score, time left and status, and an overlay on round end.
10	7. Expose `window.__

content.thinking: Right, node_modules is off-limits per llms.txt. I'll instead check the setScale/setVisible/setMaterial signatures in runtimeNodes.js directly.

Since setPosition, setScale, setVisible, and setMaterial are all available, I'm planning to avoid material complexity by using pre-made nodes per cell: a pedestal cylinder, a dark hole disc, an emissive yellow lantern sphere, a dark red bomb sphere, and a torus hover ring, plus flash burst nodes, toggling visibility and animating position for reveals.

For picking, I'll skip built-in raycast and do custom math instead, using a slab test against each cell's vertical bounding box (accounting for raised lantern height) against the camera ray, picking the nearest intersecting cell -- this handles both resting and popped-up lantern states and works well for headless click testing too.

I'll attach pointerdown directly to the canvas and use getBoundingClientRect for coordinate mapping. For layout, the HUD sits as a normal DOM element below the canvas, while the round-end overlay is absolutely positioned on top of the canvas (blocking clicks while visible), and I'll keep a ready-state overlay with a Start button too, even though Enter should also work.

For the core loop, I'm stepping time using a clamped dt and seeding spawns with a mulberry32 PRNG, pulling the seed from a URL query param or falling back to a default.

I'm settling on reusing the same seed on restart so repeated seeds give consistent spawn order, keeping mostly one active lantern at a time with a short randomized gap between spawns, and scaling duration down as score increases (with bombs sharing the same duration logic and a modest spawn probability) so that hitting the point target within the time limit stays feasible. The raise/hide animation uses an eased vertical offset over a short transition.

Each cell tracks an item's kind and age against its lifespan, counting as active (and poppable) from the moment it spawns through the rise, hold, and drop phases, while anything mid-drop or already gone counts as a miss. Popping removes the item immediately and triggers a small burst effect, which I'll implement using a pool of reusable particle nodes spawned at the cell's position with outward velocities and shrinking scale, alongside a separate flashing ring effect for misses.

For hover feedback, I'm adding a ring per cell that lights up with emissive color when hovered, matching the glowing material style I'll use for lanterns, and I should double check the exact emissive material signature in the API docs before writing that part.

I'm reconsidering the hover ring shape—opting for a thin flat cylinder instead of a torus, since I'm unsure how size parameters work for torus primitives, and working out how cylinder dimensions map to radius and height.

For hiding nodes, I'm figuring out a trick where pedestals are solid cylinders that conceal the lantern sphere inside them until it rises above the pedestal's top, so I can avoid separate visibility toggling logic. I'm also defining the clickable hit box bounds per cell and starting to work out the camera ray math using forward, right, and up vectors derived from camera and target positions.

Now I'm computing the NDC coordinates and ray direction using field of view and aspect ratio, and double-checking grid spacing and camera frustum extents so all cells remain visible at the given distance. I'm also setting up pointer hover detection by testing the same hit box per cell, and planning keyboard shortcuts like Enter to start and R to restart.

For the round logic, I'm defining the playing state with a 45-second countdown, handling timeout and bomb-click as loss conditions, and clearing items once the round ends. I'm also setting up a delta-time-based timer and exposing the game state through a global object that updates each frame.

For visuals, I'm building a pool of particle spheres for pop and explosion effects, plus per-cell flash discs for misses and hover states, with gold tones for successful pops and red flashes for bombs and misses. Lighting uses hemisphere and directional lights with shadows against a dark background, plus a bloom effect, and I'm now working through per-frame updates for lantern and bomb node positions.

I'll make the lantern gold/amber and give the bomb a contrasting dark purple-black body with a red emissive glow so they're visually distinct.

Now I'm planning the overlay UI: a centered div with a semi-transparent dark background showing a title, message, and buttons that change based on game state (ready/ended), plus a HUD below the canvas displaying score, time, and status.

I'm double-checking the remaining pieces: the ready signal fires after the first frame draws, the burst's random visuals don't affect spawn order, bomb clicks correctly score zero and end the round, and the hover node's visibility toggling per frame looks solid. input.summary:
I wrote the Lantern Pop game in `src/main.ts`. It typechecks, but I couldn't run it in a browser here, so none of the gameplay or picking has been tested.

- **Scene:** a 3×3 grid of pedestals with a perspective camera and bloom. One gold lantern at a time rises from a random cell, or occasionally a dark purple bomb with a red glow. Display time starts at 1.5 s and shrinks with score, down to 0.6 s.
- **Input:** click picking and hover are my own ray-vs-box math against the fixed camera, not an engine picking call. The math assumes the engine treats `fov` as vertical degrees. If it doesn't, the click and hover cells will be off.
- **Scoring:** a pop gives +10 and a spark burst. Clicking an empty cell or a lowered lantern costs 5 (floored at 0) and flashes a red disc. A bomb ends the run as `lost`. A hover ring marks the cell under the pointer.
- **Round flow:** the game starts in `ready`. Enter or the Start button begins a 45 s round, which ends `won` at 150 points or more and `lost` otherwise. R or the Restart button begins a new round at any time.
- **Seed:** spawn order comes from a seeded generator (default 20240607, or `?seed=N` in the URL). It is reseeded on every start, so a seed repeats the same spawns. The burst particles use `Math.random`, which only affects visuals.
- **HUD and state:** the DOM HUD below the canvas shows score, time and status. A start/end overlay sits on top of the canvas. `window.__TASK_STATE__` is updated every frame, and `window.__TASK_READY__` is set after `app.ready()`.
